properties.name: A prose field that swallowed the next parameter says so, and the write still lands
properties.rationale:
It keys on the LOSS, not on the syntax, and that distinction was measured before any code was written rather than argued afterwards.

The decision's own counter-argument to the naive form is fatal and correct: three nodes in this design quote `</decision>` and `<parameter name=` deliberately — including the decision documenting the defect and the two findings behind it. Tested against the committed export:

    "contains the markup at all"                   3 false positives
    "names a parameter the node lacks"             2  (both TemporalFacts — a type with no `rationale` at all)
    scoped to the tool's OWN declared parameters   0  across 1,776 nodes

⭐ THE DECISION HAD ALREADY SPECIFIED THIS SHAPE and nobody had noticed. Option A's counter reads: "Any guard has to key on SHAPE — markup at the TAIL of a value, immediately followed by what parses as another parameter name — not on the strings appearing at all." That was arrived at independently on 2026-08-31 from the false-positive test, and then found already written in August. The build is A's keying with B's severity.

🛑 `create_node` IS OUT OF SCOPE BY DESIGN, NOT BY OMISSION, and the reasoning is recorded at the call site so nobody reads it as a gap. Its `props` is one JSON bag declaring no prose parameters, so "was the named parameter supplied?" has no meaning there — and that scoping is exactly what took the middle row above from 2 false positives to 0. Measured the same day: zero instances of the damage shape from ANY writer across 3,528 nodes; `create_node` already carries `undeclared` and a JSON parse that refuses structural corruption loudly. Option C, a CI scan over the committed export, remains available and is the right home for that case if an instance ever appears.

📌 FIVE OF THE SEVEN OBSERVED INSTANCES WERE reflow2's OWN; TWO WERE A CONSUMER'S. `proj:bhome` hit it on both wired tools and independently proposed the same warn-don't-reject fix, which is what moved the decision off the shelf — the node had held itself below field-reported work on the explicit ground that no user had reported it.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Built the guard `dec:idea-a-prose-field-silently-absorbed-tool-call-markup` accepted the same day: `absorbed_markup()` in capture.rs, surfaced as a fourth advisory block beside `search_first` and `revision`, wired into `add_decision` and `add_change_event` — the two tools with observed instances. It fires when a prose field names a parameter THIS tool declares and THIS call did not supply. It WARNS and never refuses; the node lands either way. Five tests, all observed failing before the guard existed, and the two counterweights passed from the start because absence-of-block was already the correct answer for correct work. Full crate suite 39/39, toolsnaps unchanged (no schema moved), skill lint clean.
